1. apparently it doesn't make sense to run the sepo tests for downstream forked repos. 
2. what's the best way to disable it? 
    - adding a repo name gate? 
    - or ...?

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
Recommended: add a fork-aware job gate to `test-scripts.yml`, not a hard `github.repository == 'self-evolving/repo'` repo-name gate.

Why:
- [`test-scripts.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/test-scripts.yml#L3-L9) currently runs on every PR and manual dispatch.
- The actual Sepo CI lanes are the `.agent` scripts: build, runtime tests, workflow checks, docs checks, shell checks in [`package.json`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/package.json#L6-L14).
- Docs currently say `test-scripts.yml` is normal CI and is not paused by `AGENT_ENABLED` ([supported workflows](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/usage/supported-workflows.md#L28-L35), [configuration list](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L10-L13)).
- A repo-name gate is too narrow. It would prevent non-fork Sepo-derived repos from intentionally validating the copied agent stack.
- A fork gate matches the real condition: downstream fork repos skip by default, while upstream PRs into `self-evolving/repo` still run because the workflow’s repository is the upstream repo, not the contributor fork.

I’d implement this as a job-level guard before checkout:

```yaml
jobs:
  check:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      vars.AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED == 'true' ||
      (
        vars.AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED != 'false' &&
        github.event.repository.fork != true
      )
```

That gives:
- non-fork repos: run by default
- fork repos: skip PR CI by default
- fork repos that really want Sepo CI: set `AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED=true`
- any repo that wants to disable it: set `AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED=false`
- manual `workflow_dispatch`: still available for explicit debugging

Execution plan:
1. Add the job-level `if` to [`test-scripts.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/test-scripts.yml#L7-L9).
2. Update docs where current behavior is described: [`supported-workflows.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/usage/supported-workflows.md#L28-L35) and [`configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L10-L13).
3. Update the workflow envelope test that currently asserts the old behavior in [`envelope.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L560-L620).
4. Run `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci`.

Recommended next step: approve an `/implement` for the fork-aware `test-scripts.yml` gate plus docs/test updates.

1. for repo forks: i think people use it as a template -> can they detect it? 
2. should it be automatically skipped if no files changed in .agent (can that be a simple gate?

I still think we should remove this by default 

@sepo-agent /answer

Yes, that changes the recommendation: use a canonical-repository gate. The documented setup is **Use this template** ([README](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/README.md#L11-L14)), and template-created repositories are independent repositories, not forks. GitHub gives them unrelated histories. GitHub’s API can expose `template_repository`, but detecting ancestry is unnecessary and would miss manual copies or installer-created repos. ([GitHub template docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-template-repository), [repository API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos))

I’d make automatic Sepo CI source-only, with downstream opt-in and manual debugging:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - ".agent/**"
      - ".github/actions/**"
      - ".github/prompts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/**"
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      github.repository == 'self-evolving/repo' ||
      vars.AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED == 'true'
```

Using only `.agent/**` would be incomplete. The suite also parses workflows/actions and validates prompts and action shell scripts ([validation test](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/workflow-action-validation.test.ts#L20-L27), [test scripts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/package.json#L10-L14)).

Result:

- `self-evolving/repo`: runs automatically, only for Sepo-owned changes.
- Forks, template repos, installed repos, and manual copies: no automatic Sepo CI.
- Downstream Sepo developers: opt in with `AGENT_TEST_SCRIPTS_ENABLED=true`.
- Anyone: can still run `workflow_dispatch` explicitly.
- Fork PRs targeting `self-evolving/repo`: still run because the workflow executes in the upstream repository context.

One caveat: GitHub leaves a required check pending when its entire workflow is skipped by a `paths` filter. This repository currently does not require that check; if it becomes required, use a tiny always-running change-detection job and conditionally skip only the heavy test job. ([GitHub required-check behavior](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/collaborating-on-repositories-with-code-quality-features/troubleshooting-required-status-checks))

Implementation would update `test-scripts.yml`, its envelope assertions, and the two workflow/configuration docs. Approve with `/implement` and I’ll make that change.

can we do a composite condition: 

1. if it's sepo: track all the three paths 
2. if it is not sepo, track only .agent path 

@sepo-agent /answer

Yes, for deciding whether the full test job runs. GitHub does not support repository-dependent expressions inside `pull_request.paths`; those patterns are static. ([workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore))

The composite rule is:

```text
manual_dispatch
OR .agent_changed
OR (is_self_evolving_repo AND sepo_github_files_changed)
```

Keep the trigger as the union:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - ".agent/**"
      - ".github/actions/**"
      - ".github/prompts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/**"
  workflow_dispatch:
```

Then add a lightweight `changes` job that lists PR files and emits `agent_changed` and `sepo_github_changed`. The test job becomes:

```yaml
check:
  needs: changes
  if: >-
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
    needs.changes.outputs.agent_changed == 'true' ||
    (
      github.repository == 'self-evolving/repo' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.sepo_github_changed == 'true'
    )
```

The gate can use `actions/github-script@v7` with `github.rest.pulls.listFiles`, including pagination. That API requires only pull-request read access, and the repository already uses the same `github-script` and pagination pattern in [`agent-branch-cleanup.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-branch-cleanup.yml#L37-L60). ([GitHub files API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests-files))

Behavior:

- `self-evolving/repo`: full tests for `.agent/**` or the three Sepo `.github/**` areas.
- Downstream repo: full tests only for `.agent/**`.
- Manual dispatch: always runs.
- Downstream `.github/**` change: only the cheap gate runs; npm install/build/tests are skipped.

If “track only `.agent/**`” means no workflow run whatsoever for downstream `.github/**` changes, that cannot be expressed in one shared workflow because event path filters are static. The source-only workflow would need to be excluded from downstream distributions. For the current template layout, the lightweight gate is the cleanest implementation.

The implementation plan is to add the gate, condition the existing `check` job, update envelope tests/docs, and run `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci`. Approve with `/implement` to proceed.
